payload.claim: The spec's practice of dating "every line below was read at" an earlier commit (`f681ad39`) than the actual base it runs against (`1a0f27155fec1b2cb6a6cb8fbf9127a044a6db6e`) is worth a person's attention in general. In this instance the only file that moved in the interim (`cli.py`) is out of scope and the drift is cosmetic, but a future instance of this pattern might involve a file the spec actually instructs the cell to edit having changed between the commit the author read and the real base, silently staling a "the current code says X" claim. A human should decide whether this authoring practice is acceptable rather than it being baked silently into spec-authoring habit.
